brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level fabric string is 'TPU laminate (shiny welded) on Z Adventure line + polyester 600-840D (matte woven) on Z Traveler touring line'. This is CORRECT for the two 'Z Adventure' products reviewed - Z Adventure R17 ('TPU 420D + Polyester 640D + Hypalon') and Z Adventure Dry Bag 6L ('Polyester 420D TPU') - and CORRECT for Z Traveler 60 ('Polyester 840D', matte, no TPU, top of the stated D range). It is only a PARTIAL match for Z Traveler S20: maker material is 'Polyester 600D + TPU' - the 600D matches the Traveler clause, but this product ALSO carries a TPU component the brand string reserves for the Adventure line only; the string doesn't anticipate a blended Traveler product. It does NOT cover two products at all: Z Light Pack S and Z Frame Pack are both 'Polyester 420 D Ripstop' - a lighter-weight ripstop that is neither the Z Adventure TPU laminate nor the 600-840D Z Traveler weight; both belong to lines the brand string simply doesn't mention (Z Light / plain Frame bags).
brand_notes.method: zefal.com 403s to WebFetch's fetcher but returns full server-rendered HTML to curl with a desktop UA - matches the prior finding recorded in HANDOVER.md. Every one of the six product pages has a plain 'Product details' table (Dimensions / Weight / Mounting / Material / Type / Capacity / Closing) in page TEXT, no image needed for the numbers. Zefal states dimensions as three bare numbers with no axis labels; comparing all six against the existing catalogue records shows the maker's own order is consistently LENGTH x HEIGHT x WIDTH (confirmed by checking every product, not assumed from one) - this is documented here since it is not obvious and the wrong assumption (L x W x H) would transpose wid/hgt on every product in this brand. Photos came from the same page's own gallery (zefal.com/<id>-large_default/<slug>.jpg pattern), filtered to the images matching the current product's own slug/reference to exclude related-product carousel thumbnails.

Reading Zefal's own L x H x W order (established across the whole brand, see brand_notes.method) gives len=14, hgt=6.5, wid=7.0 - the existing catalogue record already had wid=7/hgt=6.5, which matches this reading exactly, so no change needed, just now sourced. products.name: Zefal Z Adventure R17
products.dims_raw: Zefal 'Product details': Dimensions 62.00 x 20.00 x 24.00 cm (L x H x W); Weight 675g; Material 'TPU 420D (+ Polyester 640D + Hypalon)'; Capacity 17L; Closing 'Roll top'; Maximum load 5kg. Description: 'a volume that can be adjusted from 8 to 17 litres'.
products.dims_note: len=62cm is treated as the UNFURLED/maximum figure per the new rule (Zefal's own description confirms this is an adjustable roll-top, 8-17L). BUT the on-bike photo (R17_Situation(1).jpg) shows the mounted bag reading far shorter than 62cm relative to the visible saddle and seatpost - proportionally closer to ~40cm than 62cm. Box at 62cm: 62x20x24=29.8L against 17L rated (ratio 1.75, loose); at an estimated 40cm: 40x20x24=19.2L (ratio 1.13, a close, plausible fit). This is the same class of conflict the spec calls out for Apidura's Expedition Front Rack Pack - flagged in fields, not silently changed. hgt=24/wid=20 read directly off the maker's single non-range figures.

render.conflict: 62cm is Zefal's own published dimension and is kept in dims_cm per the unfurled rule, but the on-bike photo shows the mounted bag proportionally much shorter than 62cm against the visible saddle/seatpost, and a 40cm estimate reconciles far better against the 17L rating (1.13x vs 1.75x box ratio). 40cm is a photo-proportion estimate, not a second maker figure - medium/low confidence.

products.name: Zefal Z Adventure Dry Bag 6L
products.dims_raw: Zefal 'Product details': Dimensions 15.00 x 36.50 x 15.00 cm; Weight 205g; Mounting 'clip loop'; Material 'Polyester 420D TPU'; Type 'Bikepacking fork bags'; Capacity 6L; Closing 'By roll top and clip loop'; Maximum load 2.5kg.
products.dims_note: AXIS CORRECTION from the existing catalogue record. brands.json stored this as len=36.5/dia=15, treating the tube's long axis as len (fore-aft). Every OTHER forkbag in this catalogue (checked across the whole data/models set) treats the along-the-fork-leg axis as hgt, with len=wid=diameter - a straight cylindrical dry bag mounted vertically on a fork leg cage. Corrected to len=15, wid=15, hgt=36.5 to match that established convention; the maker's own raw order (15 / 36.5 / 15 = diameter / length / diameter) supports this directly. Box (cylinder) pi*7.5^2*36.5=6.45L against 6L rated (ratio 1.08) - a close, clean fit.

geometry.notes: Straight-sided cylindrical dry bag, rolled and clipped shut at the top only; the bottom carries a webbing loop for the cage's base bolt/strap.

closure.hardware: two plastic hook clips pinching the rolled top shut, per maker copy 'by roll top and clip loop'

straps.note: bottom webbing loop for the cage's retaining strap/bolt

details.fabric: Polyester 420D TPU - matches brands.json's Z Adventure/TPU clause; see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: Mounts INTO a third-party cage (e.g. King Cage / Salsa Anything Cage style) via the base loop and the cage's own straps - the bag itself carries no cage hardware, only the clip loop. Requires the bike to have fork cage bosses; not usable without one.
